verdict.tagline: Smooth horror and action blend for a gripping dual protagonist campaign
for_you_if: you want a polished horror and action experience
you enjoy switching between distinct protagonist styles
not_for_you_if: you expect a lengthy first playthrough
you are looking for a Mercenaries mode

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players experience smooth technical performance alongside a campaign that transitions from atmospheric horror into action with dual protagonists.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as running smoothly with good optimization, solid frame rates, and an absence of major bugs or performance drops.

citations.review_text:
Resident Evil Requiem is probably the most cinematic game in the entire Resident Evil series. I absolutely loved the graphics, sound design, environments, and the variety of gameplay. The upgrade and crafting systems are also really well done and add a nice layer of progression.

One of the biggest surprises for me was how well optimized the game is. Throughout my entire playthrough, I didn't encounter a single bug or any serious FPS drops, which is surprisingly rare these days. Capcom really doesn't disappoint when it comes to optimization and quality control. They seem to be one of the few companies left that actually care about releasing a polished product instead of making players act as unpaid beta testers.

As for the negatives, the game is basically split into two parts with completely different gameplay styles. After finishing the Grace sections once, I don't really have any desire to replay them, since you already know where everything is, how the puzzles work, and where all the key items are. Leon's sections, on the other hand, are much more action-focused and actually make me want to replay the game on the new difficulty. Unfortunately, since you can't replay the two campaigns separately, I'm probably not going to start another playthrough.

I also really didn't like the unnecessary stealth section with the little girl. It could have easily been presented as a cutscene instead. I honestly can't imagine who thought this section was a good idea.

Overall, I had a great time with Resident Evil Requiem. It's an incredibly polished, cinematic, and visually impressive entry, even if some design choices hurt its replayability.

8/10

It took me a couple times putting this down to finally get into it, but man am I glad I did. The main sections for Grace are tense, giving a hyrbid of RE7 and Re2 Remake vibes while Leon's sections lean heavily in the shape of Re4 Remake with a bit more of a slower pace to reflect his age. 

Game also play phenomenally on Steam deck, as I did a hybrid between that and my regular rig and found the performance to be well optimized on both (even at 5k Ultrawide res in heavy actions scenes at high settings, I never dipped below about 90fps!)

As a bonus, while the "mercenaries" mode does not return in this title, it is replaced by a exceptionally well executed rougelite alternative in "Leon Must Die!", this alone brought me back to the game and has been a source of great entertainment, showing how solid the base of Leon's combat gameplay loop is.

An easy 9/10 at full price, and on sale this is a no brainer and a great way to cap off the stories that have come before!

I enjoyed Resident Evil Requiem from start to finish. The game is polished, runs great, and I didn't run into any bugs during my playthrough. Optimization is excellent, the visuals are fantastic, and the gameplay is fun and keeps you engaged.

That said, something felt like it was missing. I can't quite put my finger on it, but it didn't capture the same feeling that previous Resident Evil games gave me. The atmosphere, tension, or overall magic just wasn't as strong for me as in some of the earlier entries.

Even with that, it's still a very solid Resident Evil game and one I'd recommend to fans of the series. It just didn't leave the same lasting impression that some of the previous games did. 

8/10

citations.review_text:
This game was very good, nit amazing but was very close, few things just were not that great which hey, some games could only dream of having stuff just "not great".

First of, Grace and Leon being 2 completely different style of gameplay, Grace being the RE7 type going for much more horror and Leon being the cool action packed RE4 style, that was an amazing idea, personally I prefered Grace but I also really like RE7 so no wonder. That you can also pick and choose which one has which camera is great too tho normally you would probably go for 1st person Grace cause it's scarier and 3rd Leon cause it's better for combat with multiple enemies.

I think the villain Victor Gideon was great even tho I thought he wasn't really enough in this game which I will talk about later in things I didn't like.

Going back to the destroyed Raccon City... I actually didn't feel like it was that bad or forced for nostalgia, it was great seeing how Leon reacts to his fellow cops and how he treats them with respect, that was quite sad to hear him say stuff about them with a tone that sounded like he really wished he could've do more.

Overall the voice acting is amazing, can't think of any character voice I didn't like, Grace was a great character too, seeing that she's a civillian in all of that (even tho she's FBI... She kinda suck at combat lol)

The new monsters were actually so good, like the white big lady that wants to eat me and gets hurt by strong light, zo,bies using weapons like dumbasses (besides one type), butcher and who would have forget... A fat ass blocking the entire hallways

[spoiler]Umbrella's Curse was a great idea, it makes total sense that every survivor of Raccon City would be infected in some way because of what happened and how much zombie bite marks they have, also gives a bit of tension cause the character could dieat any moment cause he's on a time limit and later, near the end, you can very clearly see it[/spoiler]

The game is really pretty and somehow, n…

I had a great time with this game.
Love the switch between Grace and Leon. With Leon being more action based in 3rd Person view and Grace more horror and stealth in ego perspective. 
Awesome story, awesome gameplay, awesome world. 
It´s such a good game.

Also Leon you are a beast! love you!

10/10

I really loved this game at first.  I thought it was scary and interesting, and I really loved the idea of switching between Lyon and Grace and getting both action horror and survival horror. 

Here was my problem, I played on Classic mode (Because the game RECCOMENDED that I play that way if I'm a RE veteran) and it didn't say I couldn't change it down to a lower difficulty.  Well, this ended up killing the game for me by limiting my saves. 

It became an issue in the Second Hospital section with grace.  Really cool area and atmosphere, but there are just so many enemies EVERYWHERE and some very powerful ones too (The Chef and the Screamer). With so many enemies and very few resources (I get it, it's a survival horror game), I got stuck for hours and hours in the area, dying and having to repeat the same mundane sections over and over (collecting coins, ect).  Eventually, I just decided to start using the ammo I had because there just didn't seem to be any other way (multiple zombies in one room with a puzzle), and I ended up running out of ammo.  

If I could have just saved as often as I wanted, this would have made it a lot more barrable, but I played on the difficulty the game suggested and it just sucked all the fun right out the game very quickly. It's so stupid that you can't change the difficulty down.  So, I have to start all over, but I'm not wasting my time with starting over fresh.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the first half of the game focuses heavily on horror and atmosphere, while the second half shifts toward a more action-heavy style.

citations.review_text: The first part of this game, set in a renaissance style hospital, was incredibly beautiful, disturbing, and scary. The second half of the game drops all that to be an action game in an open city that endlessly refrences the other games, with no context, to the point it drowns out the actually intresting story. It's a decent game ig, but somewhat dissapointing

A love letter to RE2 and classic RE. Requiem marries survival horror with Grace and action with Leon flawlessly. I kind of dipped out of the series save for a few spin offs after the OG 3 for PS1. I wasn't a fan of 4's action heavy approach. Got back into the series with Part 7 and 8. Appreciated the return to horror roots. Didn't quite feel like classic RE to me. Missing zombies. Wasn't a fan of the forced first person perspective in either game.

This game is greatest RE game ever in my opinion. Paced beautifully. Just when the survival horror part starts to wear a little thin Leon comes in full guns blazing with near infinite inventory space. This game manages to do action horror way better than part 4. Found myself enjoying popping heads a lot.

Other positives the RE engine runs great. Graphically looks amazing. Character models are great. Lighting is superb. It's great that it gives you a perspective option. The game has a surprising amount of unlockables considering today's gaming climate of micros. Kudos to Capcom for adding some replayability. The final boss is befitting of an RE game and I believe should be in the elite class of RE bosses for the writing and final encounter.

No major gripes to be had. Only minor gripe is Grace's fearful stuttering of every line delivery through out whole game wears thin after awhile.

It's not a newcomer friendly game. It's made for long time RE fans. I suppose you could play the remakes of the first three, then two before this one, and be fine understanding this one. Best one so far.

This game was fantastic. I was nervously gripping the controller for my life in the early game since I turned the controllers vibration settings up all the way and was getting my butt whopped in the second half of the games more action packed sequences. The horror dies out in the later half of the game like all other RE games unfortunately but I was smiling throughout the entire game. And with the ending of the game was really well done.

If this is the direction the RE franchise is heading, RE fans are eating good. And considering the completion rate of this game, I can guarantee you all of these reviews are true.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game feels relatively short on a first playthrough.

citations.review_text:
I needed to sit with RE9 for a while after finishing it to find my feelings on it.

- The game is quite short, and if you're like me and don't get a lot of value out of replaying the same story on a harder difficulty the 80$ price tag feels mighty steep in retrospect

- The Grace/Leon gameplay divide has been talked about a lot, and I'll summarize my thoughts as such:
[list]
    [*]Grace's sections feel fine if a bit slow, Leon's sections felt far too easy until you eventually fight enemies with guns at which point the difficulty spikes in a way that felt unrewarding and quite lame
    [*]Bouncing between the two is fine. Sometimes it feels welcome, other times it feels jarring like being a child and having your toy yanked from you. Do I know how they could have implemented it better? No, and I don't really care to wonder.
    [*]Both sections had their pros and cons, but at the end of it all I felt like I got half an experience with both. But rather than two different halves coming together to make a whole, it felt like getting half of a full experience - TWICE! It ended up leaving me rather unsatisfied.
[/list]

-The story is bad. Not in that it's badly written explicitly, but that nothing feels like it was revealed to the player in terms of the broader RE universe. Grace Ashcroft is explored and she's neat, but it feels like I'm running through some greatest hits of 2 and 6 instead of having a fresh perspective on this world. There's a few interesting nuggets at the very end, but it feels like small servings in a large, barren plate.

-RE has always been camp. At first it was slasher tropes, then it slowly leaned into adventure, then action. Leon at this point is such a bizarre flanderization of his RE6 rendition that I just start rolling my eyes at the one-liners. And it's a disservice because I feel 0 tension in any of his sections because of how little of a ♥♥♥♥ he gives.

Honestly, you should replay RE2 remastered or 7 instead. This new entry feels flimsy and…

Great game, had tons of fun playing a new character Grace and getting to play Leon. It felt kinda short on my first playthrough but I did notice there's more to this game that one can easily miss. This game has good replay value and I applaud them for that. One of the biggest strengths I can say for this game is how gorgeous the graphics is and the art style and direction they were going for felt right at home with Resident Evil. I hope Capcom will do more with Resident Evil Requiem in the future. But without spoilers, if you're like me who grew with the original series, there's a lot of emotions to unpack playing this game. That I can stay to the folks reading this. My only minor gripe I can say with this game is that felt alot like the formula of the other resident evil remake games in the past (ex. RE2 Remake, RE4 Remake, etc.), but atleast with new ideas put into it. In conclusion, I'm greatly looking forward to new content hopefully for this game in the future.
Game is good. A bit short, but fantastic none the less.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign as alternating between two protagonists, Grace and Leon, featuring contrasting gameplay styles of survival horror and action.

citations.review_text:
It's Resident Evil, so you know what you're getting except in Requiem it's dialled up to 11.

Requiem has you playing 2 protagonists: Grace Ashcroft and Leon Kennedy (back with his knee slapping 1 liners) 
Only this time it isn't done like in RE2 where you play each character as separate arcs but instead the game will frequently interchange between both of them depending on the story.
This leads to the selling point of RE9 (at least for me) which is each protagonist bringing with their own playstyle. To put it simply: Grace's gameplay plays like Ethan Winters from RE7 + 8 and Leon's is, well Leon from RE4. The end result is a nice balance of 'tension and release' pacing, going between feeling like a prey then to the predator.

I believe there's a free demo you can try. The demo is only a small portion from the opening of the game but it lets you play as Grace then Leon. The rest of the game will pretty much play in that fashion.

THE TWO SIDES OF THE STORY

I don't really see a lot of people talking about this, so I'm going to say my piece from the perspective of a long-term RE fan who replays almost every title every year, the 90's trilogy included. It's not going to be a fully professional review - just some observations which make the difference for me and should be taken into account while considering the purchase of this title.

The game entwines two completely different characters' fate: Grace's and Leon's. Due to that, the player experiences two different perspectives of gameplay:
- Rather passive, survival-focused segments;
- Aggressive and brutal, action-focused gameplay.

At first, you'd think that might be a great idea, but the execution of that concept in this game fails, for multiple reasons. 

In my opinion, it ruins the pacing. We play one segment of Grace's perspective, then Leon's, then Grace's again etc. until the game's very end. The real issue with this solution is that once you get used to Leon's perspective, Grace's slowly starts to feel more like a chore and becomes less and less satisfying and fulfilling. Of course, that doesn't mean there is no place for the slower pace. I only mean that if execution would be better, it would make a more balanced, less chaotic experience. 

It really feels like the developers couldn't decide if they wanted to make an action RE or actual survival-horror, so they mixed both of these gameplay types. In other words, chose an easy solution, and easy solutions are not what make games great and memorable.

There are two possible solutions I can think of that would fix this to some degree.

a) Introduce Grace's whole scenario first, and then Leon's, once Grace's story is complete. That would significantly increase the replayability value, especially if you could just choose which scenario precisely you'd like to play after finishing the game for the first time.

citations.review_text:
When I first saw the trailer for this game I really thought I wasn't gonna like Grace. I thought she was gonna be this really annoying character I was gonna hate playing and Leon was gonna be the only fun parts, but the way this game actually plays out and the way you see her character act in game, I began to really care for her and can honestly say she is a very welcome character for the franchise. Of course Leon is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ badass and the brief power fantasies her provides in the early game was a nice welcome switchup and very cathartic watching him mow down hordes of zombies you were struggling to fight as Grace. You can also switch between first and third person for both characters which is also really cool. It honestly felt like 2 games for the price of 1 in terms of how differently Grace and Leon played. 

If RE4 remake is a 10/10 game (flaws and all), then this game is like a 9/10. Still an excellent game, and the first 2/3rds of the game is easily 10/10 material that's wayyyy scarier than anything RE4 threw at me, but near the end of the game I felt myself craving some new enemy types that never came and no big switchup to enemies to shake up gameplay. Plus no mercenaries type mode where I can ♥♥♥♥ around as any of the characters? A bit of a let down. 

Negativity aside, this game is still an EASY recommend and I'm really looking forward to RE:10 and mods for this game.

A really good game, really fun to play, despite some slight fumbles from the devs

Long version

1) Grace's section - absolute 10/10, I can't think of a single thing I didn't enjoy. Absolute masterpiece

2) Leon's section - Still good, but not as good as Resident Evil 4 Remake

Reasons - 

1) Not a lot of enemy variety compared to re4 remake
2) enemies animations aren't as readable, so parrying isn't as fluid as re4 (atleast in my opinion)
3) Parrying with the default axe isn't as reliable as the 2nd axe we get later

Some other ways the game fumbled (not particular to Leon)

1) no true NG+, I don't like the fact that I have to get all my weapons again. Sure the tracker is available early, but always having to grind to get the upgrades just isn't as good as RE4 remake

2) No mercenaries mode. The 'Leon Must Die Forever' isn't bad, but once again RE4 remake did this aspect much better

So in Layman's terms 

if you really liked the horror of Re7 and Re8: Village. You will love the Grace sections to bits. Grace's section are just perfect in literally every way

if you really liked the action of Re4, you'll still like this game. But it isn't as polished/ fluid

I may sound like I didn't enjoy the game, I did indeed enjoy it. But the dumb mistakes in this game is certainly hard to ignore like no NG+, and having to use another axe for reliable parrying. 

Overall, still an absolute banger of a game. I've already played it twice, and I loved it!!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the puzzles throughout the campaign are very easy.

citations.review_text:
Resident Evil: Requiem is an absolute masterpiece! The atmosphere, gameplay mechanics, and story pacing are top-tier, making it an incredibly thrilling experience from start to finish.
The only thing holding it back from being a flawless 5/5 is the lack of complex puzzles. If it had more intricate and challenging puzzles to solve throughout the campaign, it would easily be a perfect game.
Overall Rating: 4.3/5
<3
Basically two games in one, but theyve definitely pulled it off. The puzzles might be mega easy, but both the stealth and action horror segments are super fun.
